title: Relative clauses
point: Use who, which, that, where and what to add information about a noun or to mean "the thing that".

sentences.ja: 隣に住んでいる人は看護師です。
sentences.text: The guy who lives next door is a nurse.

sentences.ja: 先週貸してくれた本、すごく面白かったよ。
sentences.text: The book you lent me last week was really good.
sentences.note: In speech, drop "that" when it's the object of the clause.

sentences.ja: ここは私が生まれた町です。
sentences.text: This is the town where I was born.

sentences.ja: 欲しいものが見つからなかった。
sentences.text: I couldn't find what I was looking for.
sentences.note: "What" means "the thing that"; don't say "the thing what".

sentences.ja: 言いたいことはわかるよ。
日本語を話せる人を探しています。
sentences.text: We're looking for someone who can speak Japanese.

sentences.ja: 昨日行ったレストラン、高かったけどおいしかった。
sentences.text: The restaurant we went to yesterday was pricey but really good.
sentences.note: End with the preposition: "we went to", not "to which we went", in conversation.

sentences.ja: この授業を担当している教授はとても有名です。
sentences.text: The professor who teaches this course is pretty famous.

sentences.ja: 大事なのは、毎日続けることです。
sentences.text: What matters is that you keep at it every day.

sentences.ja: 学生がよく集まるカフェが駅の近くにあります。
sentences.text: There's a cafe near the station where students often hang out.
